attractions.name: Table Mountain, Cape Town
attractions.desc: A flat-topped mountain overlooking Cape Town, reachable by a rotating cable car or a strenuous multi-hour hike up Platteklip Gorge. Its summit plateau offers sweeping views over the city, the Atlantic, and Robben Island in the bay below. Cloud cover, known locally as the 'tablecloth', can close the cableway with little notice, so flexibility helps.

attractions.name: Kruger National Park
attractions.desc: One of Africa's largest and most established reserves, with a strong chance of seeing all of the Big Five within a few days of game drives. Both self-drive and guided lodge-based safaris are well developed here, offering flexibility for different budgets and travel styles. Night drives reveal a different set of nocturnal species than daytime viewing.

attractions.name: Stellenbosch & the Winelands
attractions.desc: Cape Dutch estates and tastings less than an hour from Cape Town, set among some of the oldest vineyards in the Southern Hemisphere. Stellenbosch's oak-lined streets and university town atmosphere make it pleasant to explore on foot between tastings. Franschhoek nearby adds a French Huguenot history and a strong culinary reputation.

attractions.name: Robben Island
attractions.desc: A former prison island in Table Bay where Nelson Mandela was held for 18 of his 27 years in prison, now preserved as a museum and UNESCO World Heritage Site. Tours are often led by former political prisoners, adding a firsthand account to the history. The ferry crossing itself offers unusual views back toward Cape Town and Table Mountain.

attractions.name: Cape of Good Hope
attractions.desc: A rugged, wind-battered peninsula at the southwestern tip of Africa, long mythologized as a maritime turning point though not technically the continent's southernmost point. Chacma baboons and ostriches roam freely near the parking areas, so caution with food is advised. A steep climb or funicular ride leads to the old lighthouse for sweeping ocean views.

attractions.name: Boulders Beach penguins
attractions.desc: A protected beach near Simon's Town home to a colony of African penguins that established itself here in the late 1980s and has grown steadily since. Boardwalks allow close, safe viewing without disturbing the nesting birds. It's an easy, family-friendly stop on the way to or from the Cape Peninsula.

itinerary.label: Days 1–4
itinerary.title: Cape Town & the Winelands
itinerary.desc: Table Mountain, the Cape of Good Hope, and a day in Stellenbosch or Franschhoek.
itinerary.cost: Table Mountain cableway costs about ZAR 425 round trip; wine tastings in Stellenbosch run ZAR 100–250 per venue.
itinerary.food: A proper Cape Malay bobotie is worth seeking out at a dedicated local restaurant rather than a hotel buffet.

itinerary.label: Day 5
itinerary.title: Garden Route
itinerary.desc: Drive or fly toward the coast, stopping in Hermanus for whale watching in season.
itinerary.cost: Whale watching boat trips from Hermanus run ZAR 1,000–1,800 in season (roughly June–November).
itinerary.food: Fresh linefish at a harborside restaurant in Hermanus is a reliable, simple choice.

itinerary.label: Days 6–8
itinerary.title: Kruger safari
itinerary.desc: Game drives from a lodge on the western edge of the park.
itinerary.logistics: ~2h flight from Cape Town to Nelspruit
itinerary.cost: Lodge-based safari packages vary hugely, roughly ZAR 3,000–15,000+/night depending on comfort level, usually including game drives and meals.
itinerary.food: A traditional braai dinner is a common evening feature at most safari lodges — a genuine South African social tradition, not just a tourist show.

itinerary.label: Day 9
itinerary.title: Johannesburg
itinerary.desc: Departure, with time for the Apartheid Museum if your flight allows.
itinerary.cost: The Apartheid Museum costs about ZAR 150 to enter.
itinerary.food: Grab a quick bunny chow (a curry served in hollowed bread) before your flight — a genuine South African street food classic.

goodToKnow.tipping: 10–15% in restaurants; small tips for petrol attendants and car guards
goodToKnow.safety: Take normal city precautions in Johannesburg and Cape Town; rural and safari areas are low-risk
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Self-driving is easy and common outside the Winelands and Kruger's western gate
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Cape Town International (CPT) is the natural start for this route; Johannesburg's OR Tambo International (JNB) is the country's largest hub and the exit point at the end

food.name: Braai
food.desc: A social barbecue tradition, central to South African gatherings across every culture in the country.

food.name: Bobotie
food.desc: A spiced, baked minced-meat dish topped with an egg custard, reflecting Cape Malay culinary influence.

food.name: Biltong
food.desc: Air-dried, cured meat, similar to jerky but with its own distinct seasoning and texture.

food.name: Cape wine
food.desc: World-class Pinotage and Chenin Blanc from vineyards in the Winelands around Stellenbosch and Franschhoek.

faq.q: Do I need a visa for South Africa?
faq.a: Not for most Western passport holders (EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia) for stays up to 90 days.

faq.q: Do I need to complete a travel declaration?
faq.a: Yes — from 1 July 2026, all travelers entering or leaving South Africa must complete a mandatory digital Traveler Declaration with SARS before their trip.

faq.q: Which airport should I fly into?
faq.a: Cape Town International (CPT) for this route; Johannesburg's OR Tambo (JNB) is the exit point and the country's largest hub.

faq.q: Is South Africa safe to visit?
faq.a: Tourist areas, the Winelands, and safari lodges are well set up and generally safe. Take normal city precautions in Johannesburg and Cape Town specifically, as with any major city.

daysReason: 9 days covers Cape Town, the Garden Route, and a Kruger safari without rushing. 6–7 works if you drop the Garden Route detour; 12–14 lets you slow the safari down or add the Winelands properly.
visa: Not required for EU, UK, US, and most Commonwealth passport holders for short stays — always confirm current rules before booking.

attractions.name: Table Mountain, Cidade do Cabo
attractions.desc: Uma montanha de topo plano com vista sobre a Cidade do Cabo, alcançável por um teleférico rotativo ou por uma caminhada exigente pela Garganta Platteklip. O planalto do cume oferece vistas amplas sobre a cidade, o Atlântico e a Ilha Robben na baía abaixo. A cobertura de nuvens, conhecida localmente como a 'toalha de mesa', pode fechar o teleférico com pouco aviso, por isso vale a pena ter flexibilidade.

attractions.name: Parque Nacional Kruger
attractions.desc: Uma das maiores e mais estabelecidas reservas de África, com uma forte probabilidade de ver todos os Big Five ao longo de alguns dias de safári. Tanto os safaris por conta própria como os guiados a partir de lodges estão bem desenvolvidos aqui, oferecendo flexibilidade para diferentes orçamentos e estilos de viagem. Os passeios noturnos revelam um conjunto diferente de espécies noturnas.

attractions.name: Stellenbosch e a Região Vinícola
attractions.desc: Quintas de estilo holandês do Cabo e provas a menos de uma hora da Cidade do Cabo, em algumas das vinhas mais antigas do Hemisfério Sul. As ruas arborizadas de Stellenbosch e o ambiente de cidade universitária tornam agradável explorar a pé entre provas. Franschhoek, perto dali, acrescenta uma história huguenote francesa e uma forte reputação gastronómica.

attractions.name: Ilha Robben
attractions.desc: Uma antiga prisão numa ilha na Baía da Table, onde Nelson Mandela esteve detido durante 18 dos seus 27 anos de prisão, hoje preservada como museu e Património Mundial da UNESCO. As visitas são frequentemente guiadas por antigos presos políticos, acrescentando um testemunho pessoal à história. A travessia de ferry oferece vistas invulgares de volta para a Cidade do Cabo e a Table Mountain.

attractions.name: Cabo da Boa Esperança
attractions.desc: Uma península acidentada e batida pelo vento na ponta sudoeste de África, há muito mitificada como um marco de navegação, embora tecnicamente não seja o ponto mais a sul do continente. Babuínos-chacma e avestruzes andam livremente perto das zonas de estacionamento, por isso recomenda-se cuidado com comida. Uma subida íngreme ou um funicular leva ao antigo farol, com vistas amplas sobre o oceano.

attractions.name: Praia de Boulders
attractions.desc: Uma praia protegida perto de Simon's Town, casa de uma colónia de pinguins africanos estabelecida no final dos anos 1980 e que tem crescido desde então. Passadiços permitem uma observação próxima e segura sem perturbar as aves a nidificar. É uma paragem fácil e familiar a caminho ou de regresso da Península do Cabo.

itinerary.label: Dias 1–4
itinerary.title: Cidade do Cabo e Região Vinícola
itinerary.desc: Table Mountain, o Cabo da Boa Esperança, e um dia em Stellenbosch ou Franschhoek.

itinerary.label: Dia 5
itinerary.title: Garden Route
itinerary.desc: Conduz ou voa rumo à costa, com paragem em Hermanus para observação de baleias na época.
itinerary.logistics: ~2h de carro desde a Cidade do Cabo

itinerary.label: Dias 6–8
itinerary.title: Safári no Kruger
itinerary.desc: Safaris a partir de um lodge na extremidade oeste do parque.
itinerary.logistics: ~2h de voo desde a Cidade do Cabo até Nelspruit

itinerary.label: Dia 9
itinerary.title: Joanesburgo
itinerary.desc: Partida, com tempo para o Museu do Apartheid se o voo permitir.

goodToKnow.tipping: 10–15% em restaurantes; pequenas gorjetas para funcionários de bomba de gasolina e guardas de carros
goodToKnow.safety: Precauções normais de cidade em Joanesburgo e Cidade do Cabo; zonas rurais e de safari são de baixo risco
goodToKnow.gettingAround: Conduzir por conta própria é fácil fora da região vinícola e da entrada oeste do Kruger
goodToKnow.gettingThere: Cape Town International (CPT) is the natural start for this route; Johannesburg's OR Tambo International (JNB) is the country's largest hub and the exit point at the end

food.name: Braai
food.desc: Uma tradição social de churrasco, central em qualquer convívio sul-africano, em todas as culturas do país.

food.name: Bobotie
food.desc: Um prato de carne picada especiada e assada, coberto com um creme de ovo, refletindo a influência culinária cabo-malaia.

food.name: Biltong
food.desc: Carne curada e seca ao ar, semelhante ao jerky mas com tempero e textura próprios.

food.name: Vinho do Cabo
food.desc: Pinotage e Chenin Blanc de classe mundial, de vinhas na região vinícola à volta de Stellenbosch e Franschhoek.
